speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You have a two-day history of fever and altered mental status. To begin my assessment, can you describe exactly how your mental state has changed, and have you experienced any seizures, headaches, or neck stiffness?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS)

Your history of taking haloperidol combined with fever, altered mental status, and the absence of typical infectious symptoms like headache or neck stiffness is highly suggestive of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. Can you confirm if you have noticed any muscle rigidity, tremors, or changes in your heart rate or blood pressure recently?
